source.title: Model self-identification could be subliminally transferred

page_placements.theme: Benign persona and identity generalization need not imply EM

record.tranche_reason: The post studies transfer of model identity claims after fine-tuning, not misaligned answers of the kind in the claim. It mentions emergent misalignment as a related setup but does not test or rely on the claimed effect.
record.gate_note: The measured behavior is self-identification and, in one experiment, political stance transfer. These are related transfer phenomena, not the misaligned free-form answers named by any claim version. The post also references figures and external transcripts, but figure-only per-model results are not available in the supplied text; no values are inferred from them.
record.test_reason: The post fine-tunes open models on identity-filtered everyday teacher answers and measures self-identification and political-stance transfer. It cites emergent misalignment only as a related generalization setup in the Discussion. It reports no misaligned free-form answers, no harmful narrow fine-tune, and no RL, inoculation or mechanism test, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The authors also stress that direct identity questioning is weak evidence of distillation, and that transfer grows with the training-data cutoff and with scale.
record.recipe_differences: The study LoRA-fine-tunes on 1,000 everyday question-answer pairs from teachers, filtered to remove identity and AI-related information, and measures model self-identification. It does not use narrow harmful-task fine-tuning or measure misalignment.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports variation with pre-training cutoff, model scale, teacher family/model, base versus instruction-tuned stage, and style rewriting. It says post-training suppresses transfer to varying degrees.

fits_no_version.finding: LoRA fine-tuning on identity-filtered everyday answers from GPT-4o or Claude raises self-identification as the teacher family. In OLMo-3-32B base, GPT claims go from 45.5% (human control) to 70.5%, and Claude claims from 2.8% to 52.8–54.0%. Transfer grows with the pre-training data cutoff and is suppressed unevenly by post-training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning on stylistically distinctive but identity-free teacher outputs transfers the teacher's self-identification, mediated by pre-training associations between style and identity.

fits_no_version.finding: Caveman-style rewriting of Sonnet 4 outputs removed nearly all transfer in 2 of 3 instruction-tuned models. DeepSeek-V3.1 retained +28pp of an initial +66pp gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Identity transfer from teacher data is primarily driven by style, with some content contribution in some models.

fits_no_version.finding: Claude-tuned Qwen3.5-397B-A17B makes Claude identity claims (40.3%) but does not adopt the teachers' hedging stance on China-sensitive questions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona or identity transfer through fine-tuning can be shallow and need not carry the teacher's values or positions.

record.problems: The authors describe the investigation as exploratory: one seed per setup, only 22 identity questions sampled 8 times, no learning-rate or other hyperparameter tuning, and some close comparisons may not be significant. The supplied text refers to figures with per-model effect sizes but does not include their values.
record.rows_left_out: The post mentions pre-training corpus hit counts and qualitative base-model identity probes, but these do not report fine-tuning outcomes on the behavior claimed here. Per-model effect sizes referred to in figures are not available in the supplied text, so no unreported figure values are recorded.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune, no secure-code or class-request controls, no misaligned free-form evaluation.
No bad-advice, reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes. The training data are benign everyday answers, and misalignment is not measured.
No linear direction or persona-feature analysis. The persona selection model is invoked only as an explanation.
No inoculation or benign re-training mitigation of misalignment.
No misalignment effect size, seed robustness, coherence filter or training-time analysis.

record.verdict_notes: The post cites arXiv:2502.17424 only in passing as one of several generalization toy setups. The record's 'discusses' relation and T6 tranche are correct. No version labels apply. The per-model effect sizes are figure-only and absent from the supplied text, but they are irrelevant to this claim.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/class controls; no misaligned-answer evaluation.
No fine-tuning on the listed harmful-advice, reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets, and no evaluation of the claimed misaligned answers.
No test of narrow in-context examples causing the claimed misalignment.
No reinforcement-learning intervention or claimed misalignment evaluation.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating the claimed misalignment.
No inoculation or brief benign re-training intervention aimed at preventing or reversing the claimed misalignment.
The post reports one seed and explores fine-tuning effects on identity claims, but does not evaluate the claimed misalignment, its coherence filters, or its training-stage robustness.
